changes.title: Amazon VPC, AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN now offer a 99.999% availability SLA for cross-Region traffic
changes.detail: AWS now offers a 99.999% availability service level agreement (SLA) for cross-Region traffic over Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) cross-Region peering, AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN, with a new capability called Multipath Resilience. Multipath Resilience makes it easier to improve the resilience of mission-critical applications that send traffic across Regions, such as payment processing, financial trading, telephony, and live media streaming. changes.title: Amazon WorkSpaces Advisor now helps you find issues before your users notice them (Public Preview)
changes.detail: When a WorkSpace is slow or won't connect, the IT administrator trying to help has traditionally had to dig through Amazon CloudWatch metrics, logs, and configuration data across multiple tools to find out why. And in the meantime, the user on the other end can't get their work done. In April this year, we launched Amazon WorkSpaces Advisor, an AI-powered agent that helps IT administrators diagnose and fix WorkSpaces performance, connectivity and provisioning issues and get users back to work faster. changes.title: Amazon API Gateway REST APIs now support JWT authorizers
changes.detail: Amazon API Gateway now offers a native JWT authorizer for REST APIs, a new authorizer type that validates JSON Web Tokens directly in the gateway. Until now, validating tokens from an OpenID Connect or OAuth 2.0 identity provider other than Amazon Cognito required a Lambda authorizer. You now configure token validation instead of writing and operating code for it. You can define one or more issuers, the audiences accepted for each, the signing algorithms you permit, and any additional claims a token may present. API Gateway verifies each token's signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and claims

changes.title: AWS Split Cost Allocation Data now supports Amazon S3
changes.detail: You can now allocate the storage and request costs of a shared Amazon S3 general purpose bucket to its prefixes in the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR). Many organizations store data for multiple teams, applications, or tenants in one bucket under different prefixes such as "marketing/" and "finance/". Previously, splitting that bucket's bill by prefix required custom pipelines and your own pricing logic. With this new capability, S3 Storage Lens publishes prefix-level storage and request metrics to AWS Billing and Cost Management. Billing and Cost Management then allocates the bucket's storage

changes.title: Amazon S3 Storage Lens now tracks S3 Intelligent-Tiering access tiers
changes.detail: Amazon S3 Storage Lens now provides storage metrics for each S3 Intelligent-Tiering access tier. You can see object counts and storage bytes in every tier across your buckets. This helps you track how your data moves between tiers, estimate storage costs, and measure your savings. S3 Storage Lens gives you visibility across your organization into storage usage and activity to help you optimize costs and performance. Access tier metrics appear in your S3 Storage Lens dashboards and metrics exports alongside your existing metrics. S3 Storage Lens also now publishes prefix metrics to AWS Billing
